title: CPR – Infant (under 1 year)
summary: For a baby under 1 year old who is unresponsive and not breathing normally. Cover the mouth and nose for breaths; compress about 4 cm.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} now
when: Baby unresponsive and not breathing normally – shout for help and call, phone on speaker
If alone with no phone, give about 2 minutes of CPR then call, carrying the baby with you if you can

steps.title: Check response
steps.text: Tap the sole of the foot and call out. Do not shake the baby. Shout for help.

steps.title: Open the airway and check breathing
steps.text: Lay the baby on its back on a firm surface. Keep the head in a neutral position (do not over-tilt) and lift the chin. Check for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds.
steps.caution: The European Resuscitation Council teaches 5 initial rescue breaths for infants before compressions. Follow the method you were trained in.

steps.title: Start chest compressions
steps.text: Compress the lower half of the breastbone, just below the nipple line.
points: Preferred: two thumbs side by side on the breastbone with your hands encircling the chest
Alternatively, use the heel of one hand if you cannot encircle the chest
Push down one-third of the chest depth – about 4 cm (1.5 in)
Rate 100–120 per minute; let the chest fully recoil

steps.title: Give rescue breaths
steps.text: If trained, after 30 compressions give 2 gentle breaths: seal your mouth over the baby's mouth AND nose, and breathe just enough to make the chest rise.
points: Two trained rescuers use 15 compressions to 2 breaths

steps.title: Continue
steps.text: Keep going until help arrives or the baby starts breathing normally. Hold a breathing baby on its side with the head slightly lower, and keep checking breathing.

warningSigns: Blue, grey or very pale colour
doNot: Do not blow forcefully – use small puffs

sources.title: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
